title: LSA: Layer-wise Sparsity Allocation for Large Language Model Pruning Based on Minimal Linear Reconstruction Error
claim: Layer importance is measured by per-layer reconstruction error from weight-level maps, then converted into non-uniform sparsity rates across layers.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, zoomed-in weight view feeding stacked layer diagrams
description: Three panels, read left to right. Panel (a) shows an FFN block and an attention block as stacked Linear and Attention boxes. A dashed zoom-in connects them to a neural-network diagram, with input X and output WX^T bars joined by dense connections. One weight is highlighted in purple and labeled 'Weight with smallest LRE'. An arrow leads to a stacked heatmap called the 'LRE Map', drawn in blue with red, yellow and orange cells. Panel (b) shows two Transformer stacks, from Embedding up to LM Head, with layers 1 to N. LRE_1 to LRE_N boxes sit between them. The right stack's layers are partly shaded to show the removed fraction. Panel (c), after a thick teal arrow, shows the same stack with a different shaded width per layer, representing the allocated sparsity rates. Colors are pastel orange, blue, green and purple.
caption: (a) illustrates the weight with minimal linear reconstruction error (LRE) for linear layers within FFN and attention blocks. (b) denotes the layer-wise LRE across all Transformer layers, computed by assuming removing 50% of the weights that contribute least to the reconstruction error in each layer. (c) represents the allocation of different sparsity rates based on the principle that layers with lower reconstruction error should exhibit lower sparsity.
abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) on platforms with insufficient computational resources remains a key challenge. Weight pruning is an efficient model compression technique that can reduce model size without retraining LLMs. However, due to the massive number of parameters, it is infeasible to estimate the importance of weights globally, and most prior studies assign a uniform sparsity ratio across all layers. Recent findings reveal that layers contribute unevenly to LLM performance, making it necessary to investigate Layer-wise importance. Existing Layer-wise sparsity allocation methods, such as OWL and DLP, rely on weight scoring and carefully designed score proxies to estimate Layer-wise importance and sparsity ratios, while enforcing identical sparsity to blocks and projection weights within a layer to avoid performance degradation. In this work, we propose Layer-wise Sparsity Allocation (LSA) for LLM pruning, which quantifies Layer-wise importance by evaluating the minimal linear reconstruction error (LSE) of each transformer layer under the assumption that 50\% of its least important weights are removed. Moreover, our method supports non-uniform sparsity allocation at block- or projection-level granularity within layers, without incurring catastrophic performance degradation. Experimental results demonstrate that LSA maintains high performance at high sparsity levels. At an overall sparsity ratio of 70\%, LSA surpasses state-of-the-art methods across language modeling tasks and seven zero-shot tasks.
